open_obligations: Check that 'a more limited class of problems' corresponds to doubly-efficient debate's need for a polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript (LIM-HUMAN-VERIFIABLE) rather than another restriction
Read p2 L86 to p3 L7 of the citing paper, which elaborates the same cost (debaters must write out the full human-judgeable argument) but spans a page break
Note the shared first author: both papers are by Brown-Cohen et al., so the critique is partly self-assessment
out.other_title: Limitation: needs a (possibly long) human-verifiable natural-language reasoning trace
out.rationale: Brown-Cohen et al. (2023/2024) give a debate protocol where an efficient honest debater wins but the full human-judgeable argument must be verifiable; the authors name the resulting restriction to a more limited problem class as the cost of that design. It is an argument about the cited protocol's scope, not a new result on it, so CRITIQUES.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Which problem classes debate protocols with efficient honest debaters can handle; holds within complexity-theoretic debate models
